en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Chapter The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Craving for Phenomena is the Origin of Suffering:
Is craving for phenomena not the origin of suffering?
Yes, it is.
Is craving for form not the origin of suffering?
One should not say so … pe … Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? One should not say so.
“Yes.
Sound-craving … pe … odor-craving … pe … [and so on].
Is craving for tastes …pe… craving for tangibles not the origin of suffering?
One should certainly not say so …pe….
Is craving for form the origin of suffering?
Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena the origin of suffering? Yes.
It should not be said thus ... [and so on] ...
craving for sounds ...
craving for odors ... [and so on].
Is craving for tastes … pe … craving for tangibles the origin of suffering? Yes.
Is craving for phenomena (dhammataṇhā) the origin of suffering?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is craving for phenomena not the origin of suffering?
“Yes.
“But has it not been said by the Blessed One that craving is the origin of suffering?
“Yes.”
If craving has been described by the Blessed One as the origin of suffering, then indeed it should not be said that "craving for the Dhamma is not the origin of suffering.
Is craving for the Dhamma not the origin of suffering?
“Yes.
“But has it not been said by the Blessed One that greed is the origin of suffering, and that greed is craving for existence?
“Yes.”

If greed has been described by the Blessed One as the origin of suffering, and craving for existence is greed, then surely it should not be said that “craving for existence is not the origin of suffering.
Is craving for existence greed, yet not the origin of suffering?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is craving for form greed, but not the origin of suffering?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is craving for existence (dhammataṇhā) greed, yet not the origin of suffering?
Yes. Is craving for sounds … [and so on] …? Yes.
Is craving for odors … craving for tastes … craving for tangibles greed, and not the origin of suffering?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is craving for form greed, the origin of suffering? Yes.
Is craving for mental phenomena (dhammataṇhā) greed, the origin of suffering?
One should not say so …pe… [and likewise for] craving for sounds (saddataṇhā) …pe…
Is craving for tangibles greed, the origin of suffering?
Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena greed, the origin of suffering? Yes.
It should not be said so ... [as before] ...
Is craving for phenomena (*dhammataṇhā*) not the origin of suffering?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“This craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, finding delight here and there—
that is to say, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence”?
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.
Is it not to be said that “craving for mental phenomena is the origin of suffering”?
“Yes. “Is it not, then, craving for phenomena (dhammataṇhā)?
“Yes.”
If that craving for phenomena is indeed craving for phenomena, then, alas, it must be said:
"Craving for phenomena is not the origin of suffering.
The discussion on whether craving for phenomena is not the origin of suffering is concluded.
The Thirteenth Chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
One who is bound for an aeon might remain for an aeon; one who is bound for an aeon might not attain a wholesome state of mind; one who has been associated with the immediate [result].
A person may enter the fixed course of rightness; one who is destined enters the fixed course; one who is obstructed abandons the hindrances;
one who is present abandons the fetters; attachment to jhāna, lust for what is unpleasant, and craving for phenomena are indeterminate; and craving for phenomena is not the origin of suffering.
